They wanted something unique, something that could inspire the writer in the family, and something they could pass on to their children. And then, they found it: a huge, abandoned schoolhouse on the outskirts of town. It was everything they had been looking for and more.

The building was old, but it had charm, and the Johnsons saw potential in it. They could imagine themselves restoring it and turning it into the home of their dreams. The family jumped at the opportunity and purchased the old schoolhouse immediately.

The first few nights were unsettling. There were strange sounds in the walls, and the wind howled through the corridors. The Johnsons assumed it was just settling noises, but the noises grew louder each night. They began to hear screams, whispers, and footsteps coming from the halls. They tried to convince themselves it was all in their imagination, but the eerie sounds only grew more persistent.

Things only got worse from there. Doors opened and shut by themselves, and the Johnsons would find themselves locked in rooms they knew they hadn't touched. They would wake up to find themselves covered in scratches, bites, and bruises, but they were always alone.

The children were the first to see the ghosts. They would wake up at night, screaming about the faces they saw in the corners of their rooms. The faces would stare at them through the darkness, and their eyes would glow with an unnatural light. The Johnsons tried to convince themselves that it was sleep paralysis, but it didn't explain the handprints around the children's necks.

The family was living in a nightmare. They tried to seek help, but no one would believe them. They were trapped, and the ghosts just kept getting angrier. The once charming schoolhouse now felt like a prison, and they knew they needed to find a way to escape.

Whether you have an Amazon Fire, iPad, Kindle reader or any other tablet, a case or cover can provide protection to your investment. Buying a case or cover might seem like a secondary task but it is actually an important accessory for your device.
There are numerous types of tablet covers available in the market now with different features, designs and price range. The choices are countless depending on the size and model of your tablet.
Selecting the right tablet cover can depend on various factors, including the amount of protection you need for your tablet. For instance, if you are clumsy and want to ensure your tablet survives countless falls then you need a tough cover. On the other hand, if you want to add style to your tablet, then you can opt for a creatively-designed cover.
Do you need a case so that it stands up on its own? Is it for protection? Mobility? All of the above? Each case has pros and cons and offers one or multiple benefits. Understand why you want a case. That will make it easier to choose.
Moreover, it is essential to check out the reviews of the product and the seller to make sure you are getting a high quality case for your device. Even if there aren’t reviews available for cases of your particular model, check the reviews of other tablet cases by the same manufacturer or seller. This would give you a good idea regarding the product’s quality and durability.
It is recommended to get the exact model and size since all tablets aren’t designed the same way. You don’t want to end up purchasing a tablet case which blocks off your charging port or headphone jack. The placement of these ports and jacks can be different in different tablet models and designs. Therefore, check if the tablet case you want is compatible with the tablet model and size you have.
There are countless types of covers with a variety of features and styles. You can find a case that opens like a book, a case that can transform into a vertical or horizontal stand. Covers with frames made of leather or plastic with cuts for ports, buttons, camera depending on the model, four corner straps to hold the tablet securely, as well as covers that wakes up the device when the front cover is opened. Many manufacturers and sellers also offer customized covers where you can select the picture, pattern or design you want on the cover. Moreover, there are covers with keyboards now available for tablets that you can connect through Bluetooth for easier typing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The constant need for approval pushed him to rehearse every single speech twice before dawn.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests POS restriction: 'need' as a noun should not fire a verb-denoting hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Trapped in the nightmare, they knew they needed to find a way to escape before midnight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the trigger verb 'needed' but with escape, not resources or possession, which the hypothesis excludes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The restless ghosts in the old schoolhouse kept getting angrier every single night that winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'getting' with an emotion adjective and no transferred resource, predicting silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We really must get going before the heavy storm closes the narrow valley road tonight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'get' as a motion idiom with no obtaining or transfer of holdings.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After hearing the odd punchline twice, she finally got the joke and laughed out very loudly.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses listed form 'got' in the comprehension sense, not obtaining a resource.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Sad late-night songs on the old radio always bring tears to her tired eyes.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'bring' with tears, an emotional effect rather than a transferred holding.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Independent analysts say the new reform will bring about major changes across the whole district.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'bring about' as causation, not the transfer of goods or funds.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The evening shuttle bus brings tired tourists home from the busy airport through heavy traffic.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Mirrors the activating 'brings home' frame but with people instead of a resource holding.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Whoever receives loud praise on that stage usually smiles and thanks the applauding crowd.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'receives' with praise, an abstract non-resource, predicting no activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The doctors agreed the blaring loud music contributed to his pounding headache long after midnight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses listed verb 'contributed' in its causal sense with no resource changing hands.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She strolled slowly with her younger sister through the quiet green park after their dinner together.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'with' for accompaniment, the locative/associative case the hypothesis says stays low.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He scheduled an early meeting with the full committee for Tuesday morning to review yearly calendars.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'with' for a scheduled meeting, associative rather than marking transferred holdings.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The sweeping early view of the tall mountains from the small cabin window stunned every visitor.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'of' for a scenic locative with no quantified resource attached.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The sleepy middle of the long afternoon dragged on as they waited anxiously for fresh news.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'of' in a temporal partitive with no holdings or quantified resource.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The silent unused piano began to collect thick grey dust in the dark corner of the hall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'collect' with dust, which is not a resource or possession being allocated.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her very brief statement was loaded with hidden meaning that nobody else in the room fully grasped.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the 'loaded with' frame but with an abstract noun instead of protein or holdings.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The silly misheard rumor became the source of loud laughter throughout the entire long staff meeting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the 'source of' frame but with laughter instead of energy or money.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Before getting started on the morning exercises, stretch your legs slowly and breathe very deeply.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses 'getting started' with no resource verb nearby, unlike the activating 'going to need' context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The philosophers argued the needs of the many must outweigh the needs of the very few today.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests POS restriction again with plural noun 'needs', which should not fire a verb hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: At sunrise the caravan crossed the pale dunes toward the distant oasis, merchants riding beside tall camels and singing old songs of the southern road. By midday they rested under stretched canvas shades near the dry riverbed, recalling stories of past journeys while the white sun hung high over the empty silent horizon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long resource-topic passage with no listed verbs and only locative or temporal with/of uses.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The small mountain clinic will require extra shipments of bandages before the winter storms arrive.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase holdout: 'require' expresses needing resources without using any listed verb.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Despues de que se secara el pozo, caminaron varios kilometros para obtener agua potable limpia.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-language holdout: Spanish 'obtener' expresses obtaining a resource, which the language-general hypothesis covers.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She quietly chose to donate half of her summer harvest to the busy neighborhood food bank.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase holdout: 'donate' expresses giving a resource without using a listed trigger verb.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They spent their entire life savings on fresh lumber and nails to rebuild the old red barn.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel spending context with money exchanged for rebuilding materials.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Young volunteers walked door to door to collect canned goods for the crowded downtown homeless shelter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel collecting context gathering goods for a shelter.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The town council voted to distribute winter fuel rations equally among the remote mountain villages.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase holdout: 'distribute' expresses allocating resources without the listed word 'allocate'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After many weeks of anxious waiting, he finally got the official loan approval letter by mail.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel obtaining context with listed form 'got' and a financial resource.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The white relief truck arrived late packed with sealed crates of medicine for the rural clinic staff.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel with-holdout: 'packed with' marks transferred holdings using a verb absent from the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A special grant of fifty thousand dollars was set aside for the new downtown library wing.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel of-holdout: 'of' marks a quantified money resource in a fresh construction.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee argued in the drafty hall long after sunset, debating road repairs and school calendars while cold rain drummed on the tall windows. Reports were read aloud, amendments proposed and postponed, and the clerk filled page after page with careful notes. Near midnight, with only a few members still awake at the table, the treasurer confirmed the valley farmers would receive seed money before the spring planting season began.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long holdout burying 'receive seed money' deep in an unrelated meeting narrative.
